name: AW9523 GPIO expander & LED driver
description: Awinic AW9523B 16-pin I2C GPIO expander and constant-current LED driver: each of the 16 pins (P0_0-P0_7, P1_0-P1_7) is a GPIO input, a GPIO output (P1 push-pull, P0 open-drain or push-pull) or a 256-step LED current sink up to 37 mA, with an open-drain interrupt output. 2.5-5.5 V, no internal pull-ups, all pins power up as outputs. Sold as: Adafruit AW9523 GPIO Expander and LED Driver Breakout (product 4886, STEMMA QT; JP1: VIN, GND, SCL, SDA, INT, RST, 8, 9, 10, 11, 0 | JP7: 1-7, 12-15; plus two rows of VIN pads for LED anodes; 10k pull-ups on SDA, SCL and RST, A0/A1 solder jumpers), I2C address 0x58 (0x58-0x5B).
eli5: Gives your board 16 extra pins that can switch things, read buttons, or dim LEDs without resistors, using only the two I2C wires.

supplierQuery: Adafruit AW9523 GPIO expander LED driver breakout 4886
buildNotes: I2C address is 0x58 + (A1 << 1) + A0: the A0/A1 solder jumpers are open (pulled low) by default, so it answers at 0x58; closing A0 gives 0x59, A1 0x5A, both 0x5B.
ALL 16 pins power up as OUTPUTS driven low (Config 0x04/0x05 = 0x00, AD1/AD0 low): never wire a pin straight to VIN or to another output before your code makes it an input.
There are no internal pull-ups: a button to GND needs a 10k resistor from the pin to VIN (or a pull-down for a button to VIN).
P0 pins (0-7) are open-drain outputs after reset; the driver sets GCR bit 4 to make them push-pull. P1 pins (8-15) are always push-pull.

LED mode: switch a pin with led_mode() and set 0-255 with led(); wire the LED anode to a VIN pad and the cathode to the pin, no resistor needed (37 mA max per pin, so keep VIN on a supply that can deliver the total).
The board's SDA/SCL pull-ups go to VIN: power it from 3.3 V with an ESP32 or Pico so the bus never sees 5 V. Pins must stay between 0 V and VIN.
INT is open-drain and has no pull-up on the board; Sparkbench adds a 10k pull-up when you use it. Reading the Input_Port register clears it.

Pin labels on the board are just numbers: 0-7 are chip port P0_0-P0_7, 8-15 are P1_0-P1_7. The two signal headers are on opposite edges, so Sparkbench wires the board with jumper leads to a single-row connector.

driver.code:
# AW9523B 16-pin GPIO expander & LED driver (Awinic AW9523B datasheet V1.1.1), MicroPython driver.
# Register map (datasheet Table 4):
#   0x00 / 0x01  Input_Port0 / 1     read-only, the levels on P0_x / P1_x
#   0x02 / 0x03  Output_Port0 / 1    output latches (power-up value set by AD1/AD0, 0x00 with both low)
#   0x04 / 0x05  Config_Port0 / 1    1 = input, 0 = output (power-up 0x00: ALL PINS ARE OUTPUTS)
#   0x06 / 0x07  Int_Port0 / 1       0 = interrupt enabled, 1 = disabled (power-up 0x00)
#   0x10         ID                  reads 0x23
#   0x11         GCR                 bit4 GPOMD: 0 = P0 open-drain, 1 = P0 push-pull; bits1:0 ISEL (LED range)
#                                    bits 7:5 and 3:2 must be written as 0
#   0x12 / 0x13  LED mode switch     1 = GPIO mode (power-up 0xFF), 0 = LED (constant-current) mode
#   0x20-0x2F    DIM0-DIM15          LED current, 0-255 steps of IMAX/255 (write-only)
#   0x7F         SW_RSTN             write 0x00 for a software reset
# Pin numbers 0-15 follow the Adafruit silkscreen: 0-7 = P0_0-P0_7, 8-15 = P1_0-P1_7.
# The AW9523B has NO internal pull-ups or pull-downs: an input needs an external resistor.

_INPUT0 = 0x00
_OUTPUT0 = 0x02
_CONFIG0 = 0x04
_INTEN0 = 0x06
_ID = 0x10
_GCR = 0x11
_LEDMODE0 = 0x12
_SWRST = 0x7F
CHIP_ID = 0x23

INPUT = 1
OUTPUT = 0

# DIM register for each pin number (datasheet Table 13: DIM0-3 = P1_0-P1_3,
# DIM4-11 = P0_0-P0_7, DIM12-15 = P1_4-P1_7).
_DIM = (0x24, 0x25, 0x26, 0x27, 0x28, 0x29, 0x2A, 0x2B,
        0x20, 0x21, 0x22, 0x23, 0x2C, 0x2D, 0x2E, 0x2F)


class AW9523:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x58, reset=True, push_pull=True):
        """addr = 0x58 + (AD1 << 1) + AD0 (0x58 on the Adafruit board with no jumper closed).
        reset: software reset first (all pins become outputs, latched low with AD1/AD0 low).
        push_pull: drive P0_0-P0_7 push-pull (GCR GPOMD = 1); the chip's default is open-drain."""
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        if reset:
            self._w(_SWRST, 0x00)
        cid = self._r(_ID)
        if cid != CHIP_ID:
            raise OSError('AW9523 not found (ID 0x%02X, expected 0x23)' % cid)
        if push_pull:
            # Keep ISEL (bits 1:0); reserved bits must stay 0.
            self._w(_GCR, (self._r(_GCR) & 0x03) | 0x10)

    def _w(self, reg, val):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes([val & 0xFF]))

    def _r(self, reg):
        return self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, 1)[0]

    @staticmethod
    def _check(pin):
        if not 0 <= pin <= 15:
            raise ValueError('pin must be 0-15')

    def _bit(self, base, pin, on):
        self._check(pin)
        reg = base + (pin >> 3)  # port 0 register, or the port 1 register right after it
        v = self._r(reg)
        v = v | (1 << (pin & 7)) if on else v & ~(1 << (pin & 7))
        self._w(reg, v)

    def pin_mode(self, pin, mode):
        """mode INPUT or OUTPUT (Config_Port: 1 = input). Pins power up as outputs."""
        self._bit(_CONFIG0, pin, mode == INPUT)

    def value(self, pin, val=None):
        """Read a pin's level (Input_Port), or set its output latch (Output_Port)."""
        self._check(pin)
        if val is None:
            return (self._r(_INPUT0 + (pin >> 3)) >> (pin & 7)) & 1
        self._bit(_OUTPUT0, pin, val)

    def interrupt(self, pin, on=True):
        """Enable (on) or disable the INTN interrupt for an input pin (Int_Port: 0 = enabled)."""
        self._bit(_INTEN0, pin, not on)

    def read_port(self):
        """All 16 pin levels: bits 0-7 = P0_0-P0_7, bits 8-15 = P1_0-P1_7.
        Reading the Input_Port registers also clears INTN."""
        return self._r(_INPUT0) | (self._r(_INPUT0 + 1) << 8)

    def write_port(self, val):
        """Set all 16 output latches: bits 0-7 = P0_0-P0_7, bits 8-15 = P1_0-P1_7."""
        self._w(_OUTPUT0, val)
        self._w(_OUTPUT0 + 1, val >> 8)

    def led_mode(self, pin, on=True):
        """Switch a pin to constant-current LED mode (on) or back to GPIO mode.
        In LED mode the pin sinks current from an LED whose anode goes to VIN (no resistor needed)."""
        self._bit(_LEDMODE0, pin, not on)

    def led(self, pin, level):
        """LED current for a pin in LED mode: 0 = off ... 255 = IMAX (37 mA typ. with ISEL = 00)."""
        self._check(pin)
        self._w(_DIM[pin], max(0, min(255, int(level))))

    def led_range(self, isel):
        """ISEL: 0 = 0..IMAX, 1 = 3/4 IMAX, 2 = 1/2 IMAX, 3 = 1/4 IMAX (keeps the P0 drive mode bit)."""
        self._w(_GCR, (self._r(_GCR) & 0x10) | (isel & 0x03))

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from aw9523 import AW9523, INPUT, OUTPUT

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
io = AW9523(i2c)          # address 0x58; soft reset, P0 set to push-pull
io.pin_mode(8, OUTPUT)    # pin 8 (P1_0): LED through a 330 ohm resistor to GND
io.value(8, 0)
io.pin_mode(1, INPUT)     # pin 1 (P0_1): button to GND with a 10k pull-up to VIN
while True:
    pressed = 1 if io.value(1) == 0 else 0
    io.value(8, pressed)  # LED on while the button is held
    print('BTN=%d LED=%d' % (pressed, pressed))
    time.sleep_ms(200)
